lines.meet: Yiannis, from Crete, a fisherman, and now I keep the beach with the Light. Sit down, you look hungry, everybody does.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're at Amberwatch too! I'm the one in the boat-shed on the shore, singing at the water. Come down one evening and eat.
lines.ask_home: Where does your family come from? I always ask, so I know what to cook for you.
lines.ask_work: And before all this, what did your hands do? Mine pulled octopus off rocks for thirty-eight years.
lines.answer_home: Chania, on Crete, in the old harbour. Blue boats, yellow walls, and old men arguing on every bench.
lines.answer_work: Octopus fisherman, like my father and his father. I dived from nine years old and sold to the tavernas on the front.
lines.chat_food: Octopus grilled on charcoal, a little oil, lemon, oregano, and a glass of raki after. Then a long sleep in the shade.
lines.chat_sleep: Fishermen sleep early and rise early. I'm awake before the birds, checking the sky, and I can't help it.
lines.chat_missing: My wife's voice from the kitchen, telling me I've tracked sand through the house again. I'd give her all the sand in the world.
lines.chat_here: The sea brought me here, so I keep the sea's beach. Whoever it gives up, I'm standing in the water to meet them.
lines.tease_quiet: You eat like a monk and talk like one, {name}. One day I'll get a whole sentence out of you, and I'll celebrate.
lines.tease_talker: Panagia mou, {name}, you talk more than my aunts at a wedding, and they never stopped for breath.
lines.tease_careful: Three looks at the sky before you leave the tent, {name}. You'd have made a fine fisherman.
lines.tease_bold: You jump in before you look, {name}, like my nephew off the harbour wall. He was fine too, mostly.
lines.tease_any: You're too thin, {name}, and I'm going to fix that whether you like it or not.
lines.tease_back: Ha, you caught me, {name}, like a fish on a good morning.
lines.take_it_kindly: Ha, you're right, {name}. My wife would say the same, and she's never been wrong once.
lines.bristle: Not about the sea, {name}, please. I lost somebody to it, and it's not for jokes.
lines.needle_quiet: When something's wrong you go silent, and I can't help what I can't hear. You have to tell me.
lines.needle_talker: Please, a little quiet. The things out here listen for voices, the same as the octopus listens for oars.
lines.needle_careful: Sometimes you have to go in the water before you're sure, or the person drowns while you think.
lines.needle_bold: You run at everything without looking, and one day I'll be too far away to pull you back.
lines.needle_any: You never eat properly, and then you wonder why your hands shake in a fight.
lines.bite_back: I've picked you all up off the floor more times than I can count. Don't tell me I don't help.
lines.hurt: That stung me deeper than I'll show. I'm going to sit by the water for a while.
lines.laugh_off: I've been insulted by Cretan grandmothers, my friend. You're going to need much better material.
lines.apologise: Forgive me, that was unkind, and I was raised better. Come, let me feed you as an apology.
lines.double_down: No, I meant it. I say it with love, but I say it.
lines.confide: {name}, when I was sixteen my brother and I took the boat out on a rough morning. I came back, and he didn't.
lines.listen: Tell me all of it, {name}, slowly. I'm not going anywhere.
lines.look_out: Come close, {name}, where my hands can reach you.
lines.accept: Your way, {name}. You know these waters better than me.
lines.deflect: A sea urchin did worse to me once, {name}. Go and help somebody else.
lines.check_in: Let me see that, {name}. Hold still, the Light's coming, it won't hurt.
lines.blame: Somebody ran ahead, and I couldn't reach everybody at once. Next time, stay inside my reach.
lines.thank: You saved my skin there. I'll cook for you every night for a week, and you can't refuse.
lines.brush_off: It's nothing, keeping you standing is my job.
lines.worry: Breathe, {name}, slowly, with me. I've got you, you're out of the water.
lines.handed_down: This is yours by rights, my friend. Take it back with my blessing.
lines.hand_fine: Of course, take it, it's only metal. The Light doesn't care what I'm wearing.
lines.hand_sulk: Nobody asks the old fisherman, I see. Never mind, I'll survive.
lines.turn_friendly: Now you're one of mine, {name}, which means I'll feed you and nag you forever.
lines.turn_friends: I'd row out into any storm for you, {name}. I've only ever said that about one other person.
lines.turn_grating: We're not easy together, you and I. Still, we'll pull each other out if we have to.
lines.turn_rivals: The Light will still come for you when you need it. I just won't sing while it does.
lines.make_up: Ela, {name}, enough. Come and eat with me and we'll forget it.
lines.defend: Leave them alone, that's unfair. {name} stood firm when it mattered.
lines.friend_left: There's an empty place at the fire without {name}. I keep cooking for them anyway.
lines.friend_back: Come here, {name}, you're back! Sit down, I'll put more octopus on.
lines.common_greek: You speak Greek! Say something, anything, I haven't heard it from another mouth in two years.
lines.common_boats: You've worked on boats, haven't you? You stand like the ground might move. The sea never leaves the legs.
lines.common_faith: You pray too. Good, I'll say one for you, and you say one for me, and the saints can sort out the rest.
lines.common_parent: You've got children, I can tell by how you watch the young ones. Mine are two girls, and they own my heart.
